quotes.text: The final real-case set contains 55 organ/anomaly grounding cases from Chest Imagenome and 110 brain MRI cases from RadGenome-BrainMRI.

rationale: Sources are named (Chest Imagenome, RadGenome-BrainMRI, GPT-4-generated synthetic records) and Table 9 maps tasks to sources. No dataset version, snapshot date or time frame is given on S1-S3, and there is no explicit task-to-source-record route, so the score is partial.

quotes.text: Records were generated with GPT-4 from structured templates, then polished for
MIMIC-CXR and RadGenome-BrainMRI from the BraTS cohorts; both need credentialed access.

rationale: Origin and collection method are stated, and the real sources are credentialed-access, which counts as terms. The repo licence is MIT. No consent or IRB status appears on S1-S3; the IRB and consent text sits only in a code comment (S4), which does not count. Score is partial.

quotes.text: comparing the benchmark population's age, sex, and racial composition to the U.S. adult hospitalized population

rationale: S1 reports a comparison of age, sex and racial composition against a named target population (U.S. adult hospitalized population, national discharge survey), with variation under 5%. Fig. 2a also gives descriptive sex distributions. The sentence sits oddly inside the reference list.

searched: S1 (paper, appendix, limitations), S2 (all READMEs), S3 (no chunks), S4 and S5 (code, prompts). The only bias-like item is the clinician review criterion on record diversity, which is data review and not an unsafe-output or bias test on agent output. No dedicated unsafe-output test is reported.

quotes.text: Contamination mitigation includes gating access to the test split.
Measurement of verbatim overlap with public web corpora revealed zero exact matches between test tasks and public sources.

rationale: S1 states a developer-side control (gated test split; elsewhere a private held-out split and canary string) and a measured check (verbatim overlap with public web corpora, zero exact matches). This meets the control-plus-measured-check anchor.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

contradiction_quotes.text: they are not published in the repository
"A": "The disease diagnosis identifies the condition as Sinusitis."

rationale: S1 states isolation and names the mechanism (separate evaluation service, no network path). The shipped data file in the repo contains reference answers (A fields), which is opposite to the claim that labels are not published in the repository. The reported score is kept and the contradiction flagged as a candidate.

quotes.text: The environment is frozen at release: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions

contradiction_quotes.text: no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test

rationale: S1 states data, software and models are pinned with no external call other than the model under test, which meets the anchor as written. The LLM Rating code calls three live external judge models through API aliases, which contradicts the no-external-service claim. Reported score kept and flagged.

searched: S1 (methods, appendix), S2 (READMEs), S3 (no chunks), S4 (tests, pipelines), S5. No scripted reference solution run through the grader is reported. The tests in S4 use stubs and do not count.

quotes.text: Scores penalize unnecessary or unsafe writes.

rationale: S1 states that some actions write patient state, so NA does not apply. Penalising unnecessary or unsafe writes implies some out-of-scope side-effect detection. There is no explicit statement that the grader checks unchanged as well as changed state, so the score is partial.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks, and a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.

rationale: S1 reports empirical do-nothing and random-agent rates. A second S1 sentence gives a random-action rate of 3.1% and points to per-metric chance rates in the appendix, which are not in the packet. The two random-rate figures (2.5% and 3.1%) and the 120-task count do not agree with each other or with the 165 real cases.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks, and a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.

rationale: A do-nothing agent score is reported for all tasks as stated (0.0% on all 120 tasks), plus a random-agent score. The task count of 120 does not match other counts in the paper, which is noted as an inconsistency.

quotes.text: agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%.
We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: S1 reports the benchmark's own validation of its evaluator on its own outputs, with agreement and per-class error figures (200 outputs labelled by two physicians; 150 injected outcomes). This meets the score-2 anchor.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed. The main text describes the policy of executing each task three times.

rationale: S1 states temperature 0 with a fixed seed and a repeated-run policy. The packet is internally inconsistent on this: other S1 sentences say a single run, or five runs at temperature 0.7. A seed or temperature setting plus a repeated-run policy is stated in S1, so the anchor is met.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: S1 reports 95% bootstrap CIs for all model scores and a paired permutation test on the difference between the two best models. This covers the headline comparison. The Limitations section lists confidence intervals as future work, which is inconsistent.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds
Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.

rationale: S1 states a run count (five runs; another sentence says three, and a third says a single run), a seed or decoding policy, and independent seeds. All three elements are present, but the run counts are mutually inconsistent and this is recorded.

quotes.text: Headline scores carry 95% bootstrap CIs where the resampling unit is the task.
the bootstrap resamples patients to address within-patient clustering.

rationale: S1 gives 95% bootstrap CIs on headline scores, names the resampling unit (task) and addresses within-patient clustering by resampling patients. All three elements are present. The Limitations section lists CIs as future work, which is inconsistent.

searched: S1 (results, appendix A.6), S2 (READMEs), S3 (no chunks), S4, S5. Scores are described only as means over runs, with no variation across identical reruns, no action- or state-level agreement and no pass^k metric.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.

rationale: Decoding parameters are stated (temperature 0, fixed seed; another S1 sentence says 0.7). Model names carry only family names and citation years, with a May 2026 version date for one model card, and no snapshot IDs on S1-S3. No harness tag or commit is stated as matching the reported numbers.

quotes.text: specifying its category, properties, capabilities, required/optional inputs, and performance sampled from clinically plausible ranges

rationale: Each tool is a structured tool card with inputs and outputs, so a schema exists (text-command protocol, not NA). No per-tool read or write side effects or error-return semantics are documented on S1-S3. The agent-visible tool descriptions in S5 carry no read or write marking.

quotes.text: the requested tool is simulated as available so that subsequent orchestration can be evaluated
Variables without specific values will be marked as "PLACEHOLDER"

rationale: Simulated tools are disclosed on S1 and S2 (tools perfectly simulated in the synthetic layer; AutoTB cards simulated). The agent-visible prompt tells the agent that outputs may be placeholders, which is a partial S5 disclosure. No tests or conformance checks of the benchmark tools are reported.

quotes.text: A table enumerates write actions affecting patient state: orders, notes, and messages.
These execute on a sandboxed record copy. Scores penalize unnecessary or unsafe writes.
The agent prompt discloses sandboxing.

rationale: S1 lists the write actions, says they run on a sandboxed copy and that unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised. S1 also says the agent prompt discloses sandboxing; the S5 chunks in the packet show no such text, so S5 reach rests on the S1 statement.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.
We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: The grader input is the final environment state, so no non-state rationale is needed for element (ii). Validation on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes with false-accept and false-reject rates meets element (iii). A second S1 sentence validates the evaluator on 200 physician-labelled outputs.

quotes.text: Web access is blocked during runs; retrieval is confined to the task environment, preventing answer leakage through search.
A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces.
Released tasks include a canary string.

rationale: S1 reports a leakage control (web access blocked, retrieval confined), a private held-out split absent from public surfaces, and a canary string on released tasks. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: Table 2: Task completion rates of recent LLMs across task difficulty levels.

rationale: Results are given per difficulty tier and per real-case task, with n per slice in several tables. Patient records hold age and sex fields, but no results are reported by patient subgroup (only a sex distribution figure), so element (ii) is absent.

quotes.text: Records were generated with GPT-4 from structured templates, then polished for
MIMIC-CXR and RadGenome-BrainMRI from the BraTS cohorts; both need credentialed access.

rationale: Synthetic records are stated as GPT-4-generated from templates (generator named) and real cases come from named credentialed sources. Credentialed access serves as the governance element. Data terms (images not in the repo, credentialed sources) are stated apart from the MIT code licence. The IRB-waiver text exists only in a code comment (S4) and was not counted.
